top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct, experimentally confirmed achievement: light-shift cancellation with Lamb-Dicke confinement of many atoms gives stability and 1e-18 accuracy that the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes do not cover, and cross-laboratory Sr and Yb comparisons independently confirm the uncertainty budgets. Katori (concept, first strontium lattice clock) and Ye (accuracy frontier) give a defensible two-name allocation, provided the citation is worded around the lattice and the achieved accuracy. Awarding it is clearly better than no prize.
